comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose significant revenue growth in their data-centric/accelerator segments driven by AI demand, contrasting with NVDA's graphics/gaming focus and AMD's broader data center mix. NVDA attributes its Graphics revenue increase specifically to channel inventory normalization boosting Gaming sales, while AMD attributes its massive 94% Data Center revenue increase to specific product sales (Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs). Both highlight operational leverage in their respective high-growth segments.

sentences.text: Graphics revenue - The year-on-year increase was led by growth in Gaming of 15% driven by higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels.
Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024 increased by 94%, compared to net revenue of $6.5 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs.

comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded segment net revenue and drivers for fiscal year 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Embedded net revenue decreased by 33% to $3.6 billion in 2024 from $5.3 billion in 2023, primarily due to lower demand as customers normalized inventory levels.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the impact of channel inventory normalization on segment performance, but with opposite outcomes. NVDA states that Graphics revenue increased due to 'higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels,' indicating a recovery. In contrast, AMD's Embedded segment revenue decreased because customers 'continued to normalize their inventory levels,' indicating that AMD's inventory correction was still ongoing or had a lingering negative demand effect compared to NVDA's recovered Gaming channel.

sentences.text: Graphics revenue - The year-on-year increase was led by growth in Gaming of 15% driven by higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels.
The decrease in net revenue was primarily due to lower demand as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels.

comparisons.peer_topic: QCT segment revenue drivers and EBT margin change
comparisons.peer_summary: QCT revenues in fiscal 2024 increased primarily due to higher handset revenues driven by $2.8 billion in higher chipset shipments from major OEMs and higher automotive revenues from new vehicle launches with Snapdragon products, partially offset by lower IoT revenues; QCT EBT as a percentage of revenues increased primarily due to these higher revenues.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and QCOM explicitly cite the 'normalization of customer inventory levels' as a key driver for revenue growth in FY2024. NVDA's Gaming segment grew 15% due to 'higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels.' Similarly, QCOM's QCT handset revenues increased $2.8 billion, with chipset shipments 'primarily driven by the normalization of customer inventory levels, which were elevated in the prior year.' This indicates a shared industry trend of channel destocking completing and replenishment beginning in 2024.
